stem: An adult with chronic kidney disease has an eGFR of 27 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent hyperkalemia despite appropriate initial management. Which plan is most consistent with current KDIGO guidance?

options.A: Arrange referral to specialist kidney care because both an eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent serum-potassium abnormalities are listed referral circumstances.
options.B: Continue routine primary-care follow-up without referral until dialysis must be started because specialist kidney care is reserved for end-stage kidney failure.
options.C: Avoid referral because electrolyte abnormalities are not considered CKD complications that benefit from specialist management.
options.D: Refer only if the client personally requests a nephrologist because objective kidney-function and complication criteria are not used for referral decisions.

rationale: KDIGO 2024 Practice Point 5.1.1 directs referral of adults with CKD to specialist kidney care in the circumstances shown in Figure 48. These include eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent abnormalities of serum potassium, among several other diagnostic, albuminuria, progression, and complication-related triggers. Early referral supports evaluation, management of CKD complications, and preparation for kidney-replacement therapy when needed. Therefore, A is correct. B waits until kidney failure is too advanced, while C and D ignore explicit objective referral circumstances.
educational_objective: Recognize current KDIGO referral triggers for specialist kidney care, including eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent serum-potassium abnormalities, rather than waiting until dialysis is immediately required.
source_document_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source_version_date: 2024; confirmed current global CKD standard in 2026
source_locator: Chapter 5, Section 5.1, Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48 (page S255): refer adults with CKD to specialist kidney care in listed circumstances. Figure 48 includes eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent abnormalities of serum potassium, along with uncertain cause, hereditary kidney disease, significant albuminuria/hematuria, refractory hypertension, acidosis, anemia, bone disease, malnutrition and other triggers.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports specialist kidney-care referral for adults with CKD who have eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² or persistent serum-potassium abnormalities, well before dialysis is necessarily required.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Referrals/Continuity of Care/Collaboration: identify when client findings require specialty referral and coordinate timely access to appropriate interdisciplinary services.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — timely nephrology referral for CKD progression and complications
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source's vague referral language using current KDIGO 2024 Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48. The final item uses two explicit referral circumstances—eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent serum-potassium abnormality—rather than an undefined 'significant decline' or a nonstandard requirement to wait for end-stage disease.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Referral to specialist kidney care for CKD progression/complications
audit_findings.source_authority: Current KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline, directly reviewed at Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48.
audit_findings.currentness: KDIGO states that the 2024 CKD guideline remains the current global standard in 2026; the focused update underway concerns Chapter 3 therapies, not the Chapter 5 referral framework used here.

claim_by_claim.stem: eGFR 27 and persistent hyperkalemia each independently appear among the Figure 48 referral circumstances.
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because it directly applies two current KDIGO referral criteria.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because referral is recommended before dialysis dependence in multiple CKD circumstances.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because persistent serum-potassium abnormalities are specifically listed for specialist management of CKD complications.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because referral is based on objective clinical circumstances, not solely patient request.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Uses exact guideline thresholds/phrasing and does not invent a referral urgency interval or imply automatic dialysis initiation.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B tests late-referral misconception, C denies a listed complication trigger, and D substitutes preference-only referral for objective criteria. Each is realistic and distinct.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A is consistent with Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48. No competing option supports timely referral.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address whether and why specialist kidney-care referral should occur in the same scenario.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is appropriate because the nursing task is recognizing and coordinating a specialty referral based on clinical findings.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked Figure 48 visually in the current guideline PDF. The eGFR <30 and persistent potassium-abnormality criteria are explicit. The item does not overstate referral as a guarantee of KRT or dialysis. No unresolved conflict remains.
